text: Debugging is an essential skill for any programmer. When identifying bugs, the first step is to understand exactly what the program should do and compare it with what it actually does. Debugging tools, such as breakpoints and step-by-step execution, help you examine your code closely and find where things go wrong. A systematic approach is important: test one part at a time, form a hypothesis, and check it carefully instead of making random changes. Logging is also very useful, because well-placed log messages record what happens while the program runs, making it easier to trace problems. By combining these strategies, you can fix errors faster and with less frustration.
